 Key Points 
 Colorado State admitted 34,004 of 38,365 first-year applicants for fall 2025, and 16% of the students it admitted enrolled.
 Pell-eligible Colorado residents can get grants covering up to all of their base tuition and standard fees through the CSU Tuition+ Promise , depending on available funding. Colorado families earning up to $90,000 can also get out-of-pocket tuition and fees back as a state tax credit for a student's first 65 credits.
 45% of the class of 2025 took out student loans. Those who borrowed left with an average of $32,519.

 What Will Colorado State Actually Cost Your Family?
 The average in-state Colorado State student receiving financial aid paid $22,247 a year after grants.
 That's against a sticker price of $34,684 a year for in-state students. Out-of-state tuition alone runs $36,113. Pell-eligible Colorado residents can get grants covering up to all of their base tuition and standard fees through the CSU Tuition+ Promise, depending on available funding. Colorado families earning up to $90,000 can also get out-of-pocket tuition and fees back as a state tax credit for a student's first 65 credits.

 How Colorado State Meets Financial Need
 Colorado State reports meeting 68% of demonstrated financial need on average. In 2024-2025, 10,165 of Colorado State's 24,174 full-time undergraduates had financial need, and their average need-based grant was $12,367. Colorado State determines financial need with the FAFSA, so how your assets are counted affects what you pay. 4,796 students without financial need received merit scholarships averaging $5,887.
 Grants made up 71% of Colorado State's need-based financial aid in 2024-2025. The rest came from student jobs, including Federal Work-Study, and $50,906,086 in student loans.

 Know This Families Cover Part Of Their Financial Need
 Colorado State met an average of 68% of financial need in 2024-2025. The rest falls to families as savings, income, Parent PLUS loans or private student loans. Read your financial aid award letter carefully and appeal it if the numbers don't work.

 Does A Colorado State Degree Pay Off?
 For most students, yes. That's why Colorado State earns a B from The College Investor .
 Colorado State students earn a median of $66,947 ten years after starting college, and 84% out-earn a typical high school graduate. 31% take out federal student loans, and the typical borrower leaves owing $18,750, about 28% of one year's pay. Earnings still depend heavily on major: Computer And Information Sciences graduates earned a median of $114,076 four years after graduating, compared with $44,226 for Zoology/Animal Biology graduates.

 How We Graded Colorado State
 The overall grade weighs payoff, price, graduation and student debt. Price counts what low-income families pay (5 points), what middle-income families pay (10 points) and the sticker price high-income families pay (10 points). Each income grade swaps in that family's price alone.
 How Colorado State Scored 
 Payoff 30% of the grade $66,947 median earnings 10 years after starting college, and 84% of students out-earn a typical high school graduate. 80 
 Price 25% of the grade $12,311 average net price for low-income families, $18,893 for middle-income families, and a $34,684 sticker price for high-income families paying full price. 71 
 Graduation 20% of the grade 68% of students graduate within six years. 65 
 Student Debt 25% of the grade 31% of students take out federal student loans, and median student loan debt equals 28% of one year of earnings. 70 
 Grade Checks
 Watch Financial Aid Check
 Colorado State met 68% of financial need on average, so families with need should expect to cover part of it with savings, income or student loans.
 Watch Financial Health Check
 Colorado State cut $35.8 million in spending for fiscal 2027 and used $15 million in one-time money to balance its budget while state funding stayed flat. The cuts eliminated positions affecting less than 0.5% of its workforce. We're watching it, and it doesn't change the grade yet.
 Passed Earnings Floor
 84% of students out-earn a typical high school graduate. Schools where most don't are capped at a D.

 Sources And Methodology The College Investor Rating scores every four-year college from 0 to 100 on payoff (30%), price (25%), graduation (20%) and student debt (25%) using U.S. Department of Education College Scorecard data. An earnings floor and a financial health check can cap the grade at D, and a financial aid check flags concerns without changing it. Price is judged on its own, without earnings. The grade measures financial return for families, not teaching quality, campus life or a school's mission.
 Notes On The Data
 Low-income families earn under $48,000. Middle-income families earn $48,000 to $110,000. Their prices are federal averages for first-time, full-time students who received financial aid.
 High-income families are those who get no grant aid, so they pay the sticker price (cost of attendance). Out-of-state families pay the in-state cost of attendance plus the difference in tuition.
 Paying full price is the share of undergraduates who received no grant aid from any source in 2022-23, from the Education Department's IPEDS survey. The chance of merit aid divides merit scholarship recipients by full-time undergraduates without financial need, from the Common Data Set.
 Earnings by major are medians four years after graduation. Majors with too few graduates for the government to report earnings are left out. Debt by major is median federal student loan debt among borrowers.
 Admissions, financial aid and class of 2025 student loan figures come from the Colorado State Common Data Set 2025-2026. Student loan debt at graduation excludes Parent PLUS and other parent loans, and students who transferred in.
 The calculator uses federal net price averages for in-state students and adds the tuition difference for out-of-state students. Borrowing up to the $27,000 federal limit for dependent undergraduates uses the 2026-27 undergraduate rate of 6.52%, and anything above it uses the 9.07% Parent PLUS rate. Parent PLUS loans are capped at $20,000 a year and $65,000 per student. See all federal student loan interest rates . Colorado State's own net price calculator gives a personal figure, and College Aid Pro can compare costs across schools .
 Data years: Earnings follow students who started college in 2011-12 and 2012-13, measured 10 years later. Net price and borrowing rates are for 2024-25. Graduation rates follow students who started in fall 2019. Median debt covers borrowers who left school in fiscal 2024 and 2025. Full-price shares are for 2022-23.
 Work at Colorado State? If a figure looks wrong, send us the source and our editors will review it.
 Sources: Colorado State Common Data Set 2025-2026 . U.S. Department of Education College Scorecard , data updated November 2, 2026. News from The College Investor.
